method: Same as E12a; only the resize filter changes: nearest-neighbour instead of bicubic
explanation: Val accuracy 0.972 vs 0.963 for E12a: +0.9 pts from the resize filter alone (bicubic -> nearest). Surprise vs the hypothesis: the gain comes mostly from the LARGE files (160/240 px: 0.957 -> 0.974), the 72 px files gain only +0.4. Bicubic DOWNscaling also smooths the crisp outline/anti-aliasing pixels; nearest keeps them sharp. Rendering sharpness is a vendor cue. Ensemble E8+E12b reaches 0.980 on validation (E8's weak point is 72 px files 0.966, E12b's is lower resolution - complementary).
preprocessing: Alpha-composite on white background, then resize to 144x144 with NEAREST neighbour, ImageNet normalisation
preprocessing_why: Error analysis: 32/41 E9 errors are 72 px images. Bicubic upscaling smooths away the pixel-level rendering (anti-aliasing, outline pixels) that may identify the vendor; nearest at an integer factor (2x) keeps every source pixel intact.
